Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS: 6348-1971 




Indian Standard 

BASIC TERMS FOR HANGING 
OF NETTING* 



(Reaffirmed 2003) 



1. Scope — Prescribes principal terms pertaining to lianging of netting for fishing nets together with 
their definitions. 

2. Definitions 

2.1 Mounting — The attachment of netting to a supporting rope or frame. 

Note — The netting direction, N or T(see 15:4402-1967 'Glossary of terms relating to netting for fishing-basic 
terms ' ), in relation to the rope used for mounting, shall be stated precisely. 

2.2 Hanging — The mounting of netting according to a specific relationship between the length of that 
part of the final rope or frame on which the netting is mounted ( see 2.3 ) and the length of the netting. 

2.3 Length of Rope — The length of the section of the rope or frame between the extreme points of 
mounting of the netting. 

2.4 For the calculation of the hanging ratio /enfif^/? of netting means that dimension of the netting to be 
mounted which is parallel to the final rope or frame, measured when the netting is fully extended in one 
or other of the directions mentioned in Note under 2.1, prior to being hung. 

2.5 lianging Ratio (E) — The ratio between the length of final rope ( see 2.3 ) and the length of netting 
( see 2.4 ), shall be calculated as follows: 



£ = 



length of rope 



length of netting 
Note — In this equation: 

a) the numerator and denominator are both expressed in the same unit of length, or 



b) the numerator indicates the length of rope measured in mesh lengths on to which is 
hung the number of meshes indicated by the denominator. 



Example: 



Hanging ratio E — -tF) nieans 

a) that on a 7-m rope a 10-m netting is hung, or 

b) that a section of rope of length equal to the length of 7 meshes measured according 
to 2.4 is supporting 10 meshes of nettinjg. 

The hanging ratio may be written as a vulgar fraction. 

Thus, using the above example: 

£ 



7_ 
10 



2,6 Hanging Coefficient — Normally expressed as a decimal fraction of the expression 

length of line 



stretched mesh length of netting 



Example: 



A 50-rn gill net, with a hanging coefficient of 0'33, means that the hung length of the 
net is 0*33 of its stretched mesh length.
